title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. Pi = Pi^_{0,3} is the profinite pi_1 of U_{0,3} = P^1 - {0,1,oo}, free on the inertia loops l_0, l_1, l_oo with a product relation. The target S^+_{0,3} is profinite with generators sigma_oo of order 2 and rho of order 3. The next page uses that sigma_oo^mu = sigma_oo for odd mu, and that the centralizer of sigma_oo is {1, sigma_oo}. So S^+_{0,3} behaves like (Z/2 * Z/3)^, i.e. PSL_2(Z)^, the orbifold pi_1 of the j-line.

The homomorphism phi^ of §41 is l_0 -> eps_0 = sigma_oo rho, l_1 -> sigma_oo, l_oo -> rho^{-1}.
- It sends l_1 to an element of order 2, so it is not the index-6 inclusion Gamma(2)/±1 into PSL_2(Z) coming from the S_3-cover lambda -> j.
- It is the surjection F^_2 -> (Z/2*Z/3)^ with kernel the normal closure of l_1^2, l_oo^3.
- Geometrically: identify U_{0,3} with the j-line minus its two elliptic points (order 2 at '1', order 3 at 'oo', cusp at '0'). Then phi^ is pi_1 of the open immersion into the orbifold j-line.
- So S^+_{0,3} receives two maps from Pi: the S_3-Galois inclusion (index 6) and the surjection phi^.

The automorphisms. An element u = u_{alpha,beta,f} of M^{!~}_{0,3} is a 'loop-type' automorphism of Pi. It sends each l_i to a conjugate of l_i^mu, has normalized f, and commutes exteriorly with the S_3-symmetries. Via that exterior commutation it extends to S^+ by:
- u(sigma_oo) = int(beta_0) sigma_oo, with beta_0 = f^{-1} beta;
- u(rho) = int(alpha_0) rho, with alpha_0 = f^{-1} alpha.

The problem. When does u also commute exteriorly with phi^? That is, when is there lambda with phi^ u(x) = int(lambda) u phi^(x) for all x? Since l_0 and l_1 generate topologically, it suffices to check x = l_0 and x = l_1 with a common lambda.

Case x = l_0 (done on this page).
- u(l_0) = int(f^{-1}) l_0^mu, so phi^ u(l_0) = int(phi^(f)^{-1}) eps_0^mu.
- On the other side, u(eps_0) = int(f^{-1}) eps_0^mu. This is implicitly justified because eps_0^2 is the image of l_0 under the S_3-inclusion: the cusp of the j-line has ramification index 2 in lambda -> j. Square roots of eps_0^{2mu} are unique inside its procyclic centralizer.
- Hence (5) becomes int(phi^(f) lambda f^{-1})(eps_0^mu) = eps_0^mu.

On the next page this gives lambda = phi^(f)^{-1} eps_0^r f with r in Z^. Substituting into the case x = l_1 yields the condition phi^(f g rho(f)^{-1}) = eps_0^r beta sigma_oo^{alpha-dot}. This is a relation evaluating the GT-type element f at the images (sigma rho, sigma) in PSL_2(Z)^.

Purpose. The page tests whether GT-like automorphisms (the 'équation des lacets') are compatible not only with the S_3-quotient lambda -> j but also with the second, non-Galois identification of U_{0,3} with the punctured j-line. Arithmetically this is Galois-equivariance of both maps. The two maps together form a Belyi-type self-correspondence of U_{0,3} (degree-6 lambda -> j followed by re-identifying the j-line with P^1 - 3 points).
errors: (4) states lambda ∈ Pi^_{0,3}, but int(lambda) acts on S^+_{0,3}, and the solution lambda = phi^(f)^{-1} eps_0^r f lies in S^+, not in general in Pi. The marginal NB on the next page acknowledges that phi^(y) etc. need not lie in Pi_{0,3}.
The notation conflates f ∈ Pi with its image in S^+ under the S_3-inclusion, written alongside phi^(f) under the surjection. This is legitimate but easy to misread.

u(eps_0) = int(f^{-1})(eps_0^mu) is used without justification. It needs eps_0^2 = image of l_0 under the S_3-inclusion and uniqueness of roots in the procyclic centralizer of eps_0. The inserted superscript '2' near 'x = l_0' suggests Grothendieck had this in mind.
Minor: the transcription's 'l_0^M' / 'eps_0^M' should be the cyclotomic exponent mu.

ideas.what: Second homomorphism phi^: Pi^_{0,3} -> (Z/2*Z/3)^ (l_1 -> order 2, l_oo -> order 3, l_0 -> cusp), i.e. pi_1 of U_{0,3} viewed as the j-line minus elliptic points, alongside the S_3-Galois inclusion.
ideas.modern_name: Profinite F_2 -> PSL_2(Z)^ via the (2,3,oo) orbifold structure on the j-line / M_{1,1}
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (modular group as triangle group); its use in GT theory is associated with Ihara, Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses M_{1,1} and the Teichmüller tower in general terms; this explicit map is not, to my knowledge

ideas.what: Extension of GT-type (loop-type, S_3-equivariant) automorphisms of Pi^_{0,3} to automorphisms of S^+ = PSL_2(Z)^ via alpha, beta.
ideas.modern_name: Action of GT^ on PSL_2(Z)^ / B^_3 / Gamma^_{1,1}

ideas.what: Requiring exterior commutation of u with phi^ and solving for the conjugator lambda via the centralizer of eps_0 (procyclic) and of sigma_oo (order 2).
ideas.modern_name: Galois/GT-equivariance of a Belyi-type correspondence; centralizers in profinite free products

missed.claim: Grothendieck imposes on GT-type elements compatibility with the non-Galois surjection Pi_{0,3} -> PSL_2(Z)^ (U_{0,3} as the punctured j-line), not only with the S_3-quotient. Combined with the lambda -> j inclusion this is a degree-6 Belyi self-correspondence of P^1 - {0,1,oo}. It leads (next page) to a relation of the form phi^(f g rho(f)^{-1}) = eps_0^r beta sigma^{alpha-dot}, i.e. f evaluated at (sigma rho, sigma) in PSL_2(Z)^. The page does not settle whether this is implied by the standard GT relations or is an extra 'Belyi-correspondence' relation.
missed.quote: écrivons que u commute extérieurement à φ, i.e. qu'il existe λ ∈ Π̂_{0,3} tel que l'on ait φ̂ u(x) = int(λ) u φ̂(x)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Whether GT^ equals Gal(Q-bar/Q) is open. Variants of GT cut out by equivariance under Belyi maps or correspondences (Nakamura–Schneps, Hoshi–Minamide–Mochizuki and others) are an active topic. An explicit relation from the lambda/j self-correspondence, and its relation to the 2-, 3- and 5-cycle relations, would be a concrete test case; I am unsure whether it has been isolated in print.

deep.surprise_reason: Mostly a routine computation, but it shows Grothendieck explicitly testing GT-type automorphisms against a second, non-Galois map from pi_1(U_{0,3}) to PSL_2(Z)^ (the j-line identification). This is a specific Belyi-correspondence constraint that is not clearly isolated in the literature. It is modestly interesting rather than striking, and may well reduce to known GT relations.
transcription_corrections: 'ℓ_0^M', 'ε_0^M' should read ℓ_0^μ, ε_0^μ (μ ∈ Ẑ^*, the cyclotomic exponent; the next page writes ε_0^H for the same).
'Cas x = ℓ_0 {+²+} [-(αβρ)-]' is a crossed-out expression with an inserted exponent 2. It is likely related to ε_0^2 ↔ ℓ_0, but the reading is uncertain.
'commutant extérieurement à 𝔖_3' is correct (the image shows 𝔖_3).
Header '415' appears to be the manuscript page number with a correction (possibly 414 → 415).
